Autumn Equinox Apple Tart

Served at: Autumn Equinox (Mabon)

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 50-60 min

Mabon, the Autumn Equinox, celebrates the second harvest and the balance between light and dark. This rustic Apple Tart, bursting with the season's bounty, is a perfect way to honor the abundance of apples and express gratitude for the earth's gifts as we transition into cooler days. Its warm spices and comforting sweetness embody the spirit of hearth and home.

Ingredients

  • 1 1/4 cups (150 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, very cold and cut into small cubes
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) ice water, plus more if needed
  • 6 medium (about 2 lbs or 900 g) firm apples, such as Honeycrisp, Gala, or Granny Smith, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) packed light brown sugar
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/8 teaspoon ground cloves (optional)
  • 2 tablespoons (16 g) all-purpose flour or cornstarch (for thickening)
  • 1 tablespoon (14 g) unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
  • 1 egg, beaten (for egg wash, optional)
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) milk or cream (for egg wash, optional)
  • 1 tablespoon (12 g) turbinado sugar (for sprinkling, optional)

Method

  1. Prepare the Crust (if making from scratch): In a large bowl, whisk together flour and salt. Cut in the cold butter using a pastry blender or your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces of butter remaining. Gradually add ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, mixing until the dough just comes together. Do not overmix. Form into a disc, wrap in plastic, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
  2. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
  3. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the chilled dough into a 12-inch (30 cm) circle. Carefully transfer the dough to a 9-inch (23 cm) tart pan with a removable bottom, pressing it gently into the bottom and up the sides. Trim any excess dough. If using a store-bought crust, unroll it into the tart pan.
  4. Prepare the Filling: In a large bowl, combine the sliced apples, granulated sugar, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves (if using), and flour (or cornstarch). Toss gently until the apples are evenly coated.
  5. Arrange the apple mixture evenly in the prepared tart crust. Dot the top of the apples with the small pieces of butter.
  6. Optional Lattice or Simple Top: If desired, use remaining dough to create a lattice top or simply crimp the edges of the crust for a rustic look. For a simple top, fold the edges of the crust inward over the apples, leaving the center exposed.
  7. Egg Wash (Optional): In a small bowl, whisk together the beaten egg and milk/cream. Brush the exposed crust edges (and lattice, if applicable) with the egg wash. Sprinkle with turbinado sugar for extra sparkle and crunch.
  8. Bake for 20 minutes at 400°F (200°C). Then reduce the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) and continue baking for another 30-40 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the apples are tender and bubbling. If the crust browns too quickly, loosely cover the edges with aluminum foil.
  9. Remove the tart from the oven and let it cool on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes before serving. This allows the filling to set.

Tips

  • For best results, use a mix of sweet and tart apples to achieve a balanced flavor.
  • Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream or a dollop of whipped cream for an extra treat.
  • Leftover tart can be stored at room temperature for up to 2 days, or refrigerated for up to 4 days. Reheat gently in the oven if desired.
